diagnosis: The Kennet at Marlborough is a chalk catchment fed by groundwater. Observed runoff (about 0.5 mm/d) is far below precipitation minus PET (about 0.75 mm/d), which points to water leaving through groundwater outside the topographic catchment. Standard HBV with default ranges overpredicted volume (PBIAS +114%). A free calibration then made up for it with unrealistic snow parameters (TT=3, SFCF=0.4), reaching NSE 0.77 with bias still at +29%. Instead I used the lower zone as a deep-loss sink: K2 is fixed at 1e-6, so PERC (about 0.39 mm/d) acts as a constant loss to deep groundwater. The upper zone, with K1 about 0.017/d (a recession timescale of about 58 days), then represents the slowly reacting chalk aquifer. A large FC (about 440 mm), LP about 0.5 and a high BETA keep the response to rain smooth. Over 1971-1997 the calibration gives NSE 0.886, KGE 0.79, r 0.956 and PBIAS -7%. A version with a slightly larger K2 scored NSE 0.90, but its lower store kept filling and its outflow kept rising, so I rejected it as unlikely to hold in a later period. Remaining weaknesses: flow is underestimated slightly overall, and very wet groundwater-flood winters and deep drought recessions are less well matched. Snow parameters are poorly identified but matter little, since only 1.5% of precipitation falls as snow. I have moderate confidence in the response parameters. No split-sample validation was run, so the score on 1998-2008 is untested.
